::: {.lead}
Today you practise using AI safely and honestly, as in Lectures 17 and 18.
There are no new ideas. **Part A** is in Word and an AI assistant on the
lab computer; **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive page: on
paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step,
write your result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word, a browser and an AI assistant
  that the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Word.
- **All names and numbers here are made up.** Never paste real personal
  data into an AI tool.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · Safe prompts at work

**The idea (Lecture 17):** personal data (names with contact details, ID
numbers, health, salaries), sensitive data and confidential information
(customer lists, quiz questions, secret deals) stay out of a prompt.
**Anonymize** with placeholders such as [Customer]; keep what the AI needs;
add the real details later, in Word.

**Aim:** make three prompts safe, and add the real details in Word.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Word and an AI assistant)**
:::

1. Three people want to paste these prompts into a free AI chat tool. In
   Word, write a safe version of Huda's and Omar's prompts with
   placeholders, and one sentence for Sami.
   **Huda:** *Write a birthday message for our colleague Lina Hasan, born 2
   March 1995, who lives at 5 Olive Street.* **Omar:** *Write a reply to
   Faris Nasser (faris.n@example.com, phone 0795 111 222), who asks for a
   refund of 25 JD for a broken lamp.* **Sami:** *Here are the questions of
   tomorrow's quiz. Write the answers for me.*

   {{< record "Omar's safe prompt … ; my sentence for Sami …" lines=3 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Huda: "Write a birthday message for our colleague [name]." The birthday
   and the address are not needed. Omar: "Write a reply to [Customer], who
   asks for a refund of 25 JD for a broken lamp." Sami: quiz questions are
   confidential, and the answers must be his own; he can ask "Explain [the
   topic] with one example."
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   May "25 JD" and "a broken lamp" stay in Omar's prompt?

   - [x] Yes: the AI needs them, and they do not say who the customer is.

     Why: Keep what the task needs; replace only who the person is.

   - [ ] No: every number must go.

     Why: The amount is not personal data.

   - [ ] No: the lamp is confidential.

     Why: A broken lamp says nothing about the customer.
   :::

2. Send Omar's safe prompt to the AI assistant. Paste the reply into Word,
   then replace [Customer] with *Mr Nasser* yourself, in Word.

   {{< record "Where I added the real name: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **In Word, after the AI answered**: the AI never saw the name. The
   reply keeps 25 JD and the broken lamp.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the steps of a safe prompt in order.

   1. Mark the personal data in the prompt.
   2. Replace it with placeholders.
   3. Send the safe prompt to the AI.
   4. Add the real details in Word.

   Why: The AI never sees the personal data; you add it at the end.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-11/sims/prompt-cleaner.html" poster="../../week-11/sims/prompt-cleaner.png" title="Prompt Cleaner: no personal data in the chat" >}}

3. In **Prompt Cleaner**, clean the prompts of **Mona** (a table of sick
   days) and **Omar** (a contract). What happens to "diabetes" and "back
   pain" in Mona's table?

   {{< record "Diabetes and back pain: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **They go**: health is sensitive data, and the table counts only days.
   The names become [employee 1], [employee 2]…
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Mona's table: what replaces "Ali Saeed"?

   - [x] [employee 1]

     Why: A placeholder hides who the person is.

   - [ ] Ali S.

     Why: A short name still shows who the person is.

   - [ ] nothing: the AI is private

     Why: A free chat tool may keep and use what you paste.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Five steps and a statement

**The idea (Lectures 17 and 18):** five steps for responsible AI use:
remove personal data; check the rules of the tool; respect copyright;
check the output; state the use. An **AI-use statement** names the tool,
what the AI did, what you changed and how you checked it.

**Aim:** plan Rana's poster with the five steps, and write her statement.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Rana makes a poster for the new teas of the Sunrise shop with an AI
   tool. Her plan: paste the supplier's catalogue page (its text and
   photo), paste the price list of the regular customers with their
   names, ask for "a nice text", and use the AI picture as it is. In Word,
   write one sentence for each of the five steps for Rana.

   {{< record "My sentence for copyright: …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good plan: 1 no names of customers; 2 an allowed tool and its terms of
   use for images; 3 do not upload the supplier's text and photo: describe
   the teas in her own words; 4 check every price and fact against the
   shop's list; 5 state the use.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which of the five steps fixes each part of Rana's plan? Sort them.

   Remove personal data
   :   the price list of the customers, with their names

       Why: The poster needs no customer names.

   Respect copyright
   :   the supplier's catalogue text and photo

       Why: They belong to the supplier.

   Check the output
   :   the AI picture used as it is

       Why: Check the picture and every price before you use it.

   State the use
   :   nobody knows that AI helped

       Why: A short statement says what the AI did.
   :::

2. Write Rana's AI-use statement in two or three sentences, under her
   plan.

   {{< record "Rana's statement" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   For example: "Text draft and picture made with an AI tool. Prices and
   facts checked by Rana against the shop's list."
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which statement is honest and complete?

   - [x] Text draft and picture made with an AI tool. Prices and facts checked by Rana.

     Why: It says what the AI did and how Rana checked it.

   - [ ] AI was used.

     Why: For what? And who checked it?

   - [ ] Made by Rana.

     Why: Not honest: the AI made the draft and the picture.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-11/sims/responsible-or-not.html" poster="../../week-11/sims/responsible-or-not.png" title="Responsible or Not? Six people, six AI tasks" kind="game" >}}

3. Play **Responsible or Not?**. What is your judgement of the colleague
   who uploads a paid e-book to an AI tool to turn it into a company guide?

   {{< record "The e-book: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Not OK**: the book is protected by copyright. Rana's poster with an AI
   image tool is fine when she checks the tool's terms of use.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Rana makes a poster for the shop with an AI image tool. What is your
   judgement?

   - [x] Fine: check the tool's terms of use.

     Why: The terms say what you may do with the pictures.

   - [ ] Never allowed.

     Why: AI pictures are allowed when the rules of the tool allow your use.

   - [ ] Fine: AI pictures have no rules.

     Why: Every tool has terms of use.
   :::
